evidence: REACHABILITY. Runtime: environment/Dockerfile installs node:22-bookworm-slim with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally and NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, matching integration.md ('Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH; use only those packages and Node built-ins'). Sessions, password checks (crypto), polling/SSE live updates, SQLite persistence and static UI are all buildable with those plus built-ins; network is public (task.toml network_mode="public"), CDN allowed by instruction.md line 13. Launch contract in tests/test.sh lines 97-111 (env -i with PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT=3000, DB_PATH; uid 65534; possible /tmp/submission copy) is exactly what hireops_rules.md section 8 and instruction.md lines 13-15 tell the agent. Seed: every account named in instruction.md line 17 exists in seed users with the stated roles; candidate_status_labels and thread_page_size=30 are in the seed as rules section 9 says; APP-101 has 120 messages with unique, sorted created_at (so 'most recent 30, oldest first' and 30-at-a-time paging are well defined); read markers resolve: Mei Lin (USR-REC2) read_count 1 on APP-201 whose messages 2-3 are from Tomas (USR-CAN2), giving exactly the '2 unread' that hro_unread_counts quotes; candidate emails on APP-101/302/201/301 link the three candidate accounts. Every graded behaviour in functional/judge.toml traces to an explicit rule (one-stage moves, reject reason/Hired, reopen-to-origin with reason cleared and restored by undo, interview limit incl. bulk and undo, 409 version conflict naming who, optimistic put-back with focus on the card, bulk board-order arrival, undo once/conflict, activity kinds/newest first/job filter, notes permissions, 15 s live updates, Enter/Shift+Enter, paging, unread/seen, drafts, candidate wording/privacy/404, 401/403, restart). The scripted golden run (raw-evidence-index, hashes verified) reports all 18 groups passed, which shows the rules are jointly satisfiable; it is not a configured judge run. AMBIGUITIES FOUND (reported per the row): (1) Whether a re-order is a 'move' for undo. hireops_rules.md section 3 Undo: 'A person can undo their own most recent move ... an earlier move is no longer undoable once the same person has made a later one', while the same section lists changes as 'moved, re-ordered, rejected or reopened' as distinct verbs. The functional protocol B(11) and hro_undo_once grade the reading that a re-order is a later move ('As Rafael move Y up one place, then check that the V-and-X move is no longer offered for undo'); the golden (index.js lines 165-168, 307, 337) records re-orders as actions and so supersedes. The dominant reading is well supported by the rules' own wording ('A card can be moved up or down within its stage'; hiring manager 'may move cards ... including re-ordering'; version 'changes whenever the card moves'), so this is a minor second reading rather than a contradiction. Bounded impact: X was already moved by Mei in B(9), so the V-and-X undo is refused under either reading and the criterion text ('no longer undoable. Fails if either is possible') is satisfied; only the protocol's stricter 'no longer offered' wording could fail a reading-A app that still shows an Undo control that then refuses. (2) 'place it came from' for undo when other cards in the origin stage changed meanwhile (index vs relative position) is unspecified; not exercised adversely, since every graded undo (B(1), B(4), M reopen) happens before neighbours change. (3) Whether a neighbour's re-order counts as 'this card re-ordered' for undo conflict is unspecified; not graded. (4) How a session 'ends' for the draft rule is unspecified (no session lifetime stated); explicit sign-out vs expiry not graded. (5) Hiring-manager visibility of other jobs' boards/activity/notes is not stated; criteria grade only offered/refused actions, so both readings pass. (6) ESM 'import' ignores NODE_PATH; integration.md's 'available through NODE_PATH' points to require/createRequire and the agent can verify locally - reachable, not a defect. None of items 2-6 changes a grade for a conforming reading. Cross-row observations (not decided here): hro_unread_counts hard-codes Mei's starting 2 although Mei opens Conversations in protocol T before U, so an app that auto-opens a conversation could legitimately clear it (row 37); the B(11) leg is non-discriminating because of the B(9) conflict (rows 26/30). No unreachable requirement found.
counterexample: Conforming-alternative risk (minor): an app that treats only stage changes, rejections and reopenings as undoable 'moves' and re-orders as non-undoable keeps showing 'Undo: Rafael moved 2 candidates to Interview' after B(11); clicking it is refused (X changed by Mei). A judge following protocol B(11) 'check that the V-and-X move is no longer offered for undo' may score hro_undo_once 0 even though undo of that move is not possible. Broken app that could pass: none found for this row; reachability and single reading hold for every other graded rule.
suggested_fix: Add one clause to hireops_rules.md section 3 Undo, e.g. 'Re-ordering a card is a move too', and align functional protocol B(11) with the criterion's outcome wording ('no longer undoable'), optionally using a later move on an untouched set so the leg discriminates.
